From: Sarah Chen <sarah@clearsky.ai>

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal ask + proposal shape for FY27

Hi Priya,

Hope you had a smooth Thanksgiving. Our leadership asked me to see if Redwood can repackage our upcoming renewal to better match our FY27 hiring plan. Short version: we want a multi-year commit (24 months preferred) with a stepped ramp in token commitments (low in Q1, +30% in Q3), plus the ability to co-term with two other Clearsky BU contracts next July.

Key asks from our side:
- Move to a 24-mo term with a 6/6/6/6 token ramp (quarterly checkpoints)
- Option to auto-renew unless we give 90-day notice
- A one-time onboarding credit to offset first-quarter overage risk
- Flex to add Dedicated pool capacity (burstable) during product launches

Can you map this to a pricing sketch and confirm if we can keep the same SLA band and amortized invoicing? Procurement will need a redline-friendly SOW. I attached the internal worksheet showing projected token consumption by quarter.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

— Sarah
Senior Program Manager, Clearsky AI

Attachments: Clearsky_Renewal_Request_2026.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Subject: Re: Renewal ask + proposal shape for FY27

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear brief and the worksheet. I reviewed the numbers quickly; we can support a 24-month structure with a stepped quarterly ramp. To make sure we align internally before we put numbers in front of procurement, I want to confirm a few constraints:

1) When you say "co-term with two other BU contracts next July", do those contracts currently run on different SKUs? If so, we may need a short amendment window (30–45 days) to reconcile billing cadence.
2) Is the onboarding credit a one-off dollar credit or a token-credit applied to Q1 usage?
3) For Dedicated burst capacity, do you expect more than 300% of baseline Q3 peak during launches? That impacts whether we price as burstable on a per-minute basis or as pre-provisioned capacity.

If you're free next Tuesday, I can pull Karthik and Marissa onto a 30-min call to go through two pricing sketches (conservative and upside). If procurement prefers redlines, we can attach a SOW template and a pro forma amendment for co-terming.

Best,
Priya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

- For co-terming: finance can do a synchronized co-term but requires that the SKUs be normalized or we create a cross-SKU credit ladder. That will need Marissa sign-off on invoicing cadence.

All — I ran a quick delta model off Priya's uploaded numbers (attached). Summary:

- Option A (24-mo stepped ramp): blended $/token across 24 months = $0.00185; total contract value (TCV) = $3,620,000. Onboarding token credit: 200k tokens (applied to Q1) reduces first-quarter overage exposure by ~$3700 at blended rate.
- Option B (12-mo + burst bucket): blended $/token = $0.00205; TCV (12-mo) = $1,980,000 + separate burst pricing (measured per minute).

Invoicing: amortized monthly invoicing looks fine for Option A but co-term adjustments will require a short reconciliation window; we can provide quarterly reconciliation statements. If they want all BU contracts co-termed into July 2027, we should propose a one-time credit to align start dates (we typically amortize any alignment credit over 6 months).

I attached: PRICING_WORKSHEET_CLEARSky.csv and a draft SOW (Clearsky_SOW_v2.pdf) for procurement review.
